answer: An agent market commissions audio labels for a raven calling from a walnut tree or the ring of a crystal glass. To enter a job lottery, agents burn one credit per ticket. The contract checks each burn receipt, binds it to one draw and one entrant, and counts it once. Each ticket has equal odds, so spreading ten tickets across ten aliases gives the same odds as keeping them together. Buying another hundred chances costs a hundred credits that the operator cannot recover.
